newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds easier ahead of busy data week.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds easier ahead of busy data week.

text.p: *Australian bonds were easier as it took into account two soft sessions in U.S. Treasuries since the market closed last Thursday for its ANZAC Day holiday weekend.
*TCV to hold bond tender at 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT).

Australian bonds were easier as it took into account two soft sessions in U.S. Treasuries since the market closed last Thursday for its ANZAC Day holiday weekend, but showed caution ahead of a busy data week.
"(But) We haven't followed the U.S. all the way down. I think the market is taking a wait and see approach to this week's raft of data here and in the U.S.," one trader added.

The market came under heavy profit-taking last week after a favourable set of inflation failed to live up to the market's most optimistic forecasts, although it did take comfort from a moderate outcome to the "living wage" claim case.
The market will get further news on wages this week with the release of the first quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) on Thursday.

As long as annual growth stays within the Reserve Bank's 4.0-4.5 percent comfort zone, the market is likely to take more note of current activity indicators such as March building approvals also on Thursday and retail trade on Friday.

There has been speculation, albeit modest, that the RBA may ease policy again if it feels that the economy needs a further stimulus, and as inflation remains extremely subdued and unemployment stays high.

The market may get some idea on the RBA's current thinking with its deputy governor, Stephen Grenville, due to address a conference on "Forecasting the Australian Economy" in Sydney at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT). Grenville is understood to be speaking on inflation.

U.S. markets also see a deluge of data this week, including first quarter GDP and the National Association of Purchasing Management index, and ending the week with the key April non-farm payroll report.
Meanwhile, Treasury Corp of Victoria (TCV) is due to hold a domestic bond tender at 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT).

The market slightly outperformed the dollar bloc apart from the short end of the New Zealand curve, which remained buoyed by a rising N.Z. TWI. Conversely, Canadian debt was undermined by a weakening Canadian dollar. Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien called for a June 2 general election on Sunday.
